First, .claude/settings.local.json drifted into the merge again -- the PR #163 class, now five times in two days -- and was restored from origin/main before the commit, never shipped. Second, package.json came back showing 307 changed lines for a ONE-LINE addition: writing the file through Python normalised its EOLs, and this repo stores package.json with LF while the mount and every safe-write path default to CRLF. `git diff --ignore-all-space` proved the content delta was a single line, and `git add --renormalize` settled it. Diff SIZE is not diff CONTENT: check with --ignore-all-space before believing a whole-file rewrite, and before assuming a conflict resolution went wrong. R4 FOLD -- the gate refused this ship and was RIGHT to. check-script-conventions.mjs (check #63, which did not exist when #185 was authored) flagged scripts/check-upcoming-event-cover.mjs as a NEW guard with no canary. Rather than allowlist it, a --self-test was added: 10 cases driving the pure findBreaches() in both directions plus the two thresholds nothing else asserted, MIN_ROWS=50 and the PostgREST ROW_CAP=1000. Those thresholds are precisely why this guard does NOT inherit the check-sourcemap-debugids.mjs defect phase 11 fixed: an empty result is a FAILURE here, never a skip, and a full-cap page reds rather than silently truncating. The canary now runs FIRST in CI, needs no secrets and no DB. Two of the threshold cases were initially written as comparisons against the constants themselves (ROW_CAP <= ROW_CAP) -- tautologies that can never fail, which is exactly what R4 exists to stop; they now assert the named literals, so changing either constant reds them. 3-mutation battery all caught (disarm the floor to 0 -> 1 red; raise the cap past PostgREST's real limit -> 1; treat an empty-string cover as present -> 1), file restored byte-identically. ONE OF THOSE MUTATIONS FIRST DID NOT APPLY -- the predicate was spelled with a different identifier than I assumed -- and per the rule banked in phase 11, a mutation that does not apply proves NOTHING and must be re-run, not counted. VERIFIED LIVE: the guard passes against production, 736 upcoming rows over 180 days all covered, comfortably under the 1000-row cap (the docblock measured 735 the day before, so the horizon is still well inside its bound). 7/7 existing specs, 744 unit tests.
